summary: Range light at Tignish Harbour, PEI: beacons 1877, tower lit 1881, decommissioned 1997, moved to Fisherman's Haven Park in 2008.

structures.note: Built by Henry Williams under a $545 contract; relocated 2008 (Lighthouse Friends).

access.note: Tower relocated in 2008 to Fisherman's Haven Park at Tignish Shore (Lighthouse Friends). Owned by Tignish Shore Community Council; grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Two fixed beacons on masts set up to guide vessels into Tignish Harbour; erected by Theodore Bernard for $130.
Isidore Chasson appointed first keeper at $100 a year.
A gale of 29 October 1879 destroyed the beacons.
Tower exhibited its light at the opening of navigation; built by Henry Williams under a $545 contract.
Gale carried away the front light (fall 1887); replaced by a new mast and shed in 1888.
Stone foundation replaced the rotten wooden foundation under the tower.
Tower electrified; the last keeper was replaced by a caretaker.
Tower served as a rear range light until 1989 (then a coastal light, per Lighthouse Friends).
Tower moved from the harbour entrance to Fisherman's Haven Park at Tignish Shore.

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends says the light was decommissioned in 1997; the tower was moved in 2008 and stands as a relocated structure, not a working light. Check the current Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights before applying.
In 1877 the lights were two beacons on masts; the tower first exhibited its light in 1881 (Lighthouse Friends). The 1877 date fits the beacons, not the tower.

Lighthouse Friends gives the relocated tower's position in Fisherman's Haven Park. The record's position may be the pre-2008 harbour-entrance site, about 540 m away by our arithmetic. Human check before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives Iso G 1s (green). Lighthouse Friends describes the 1881 tower light as fixed white. The sources read do not give the characteristic in use before 1997, nor any later one, so the record's value is not confirmed or refuted here. Check the Coast Guard list.
The record notes that sources differ on whether the light is still lit. Lighthouse Friends says decommissioned 1997, which the story follows.
Agate Gaudet (Lighthouse Friends) and Agape Gaudet (Department of Marine table, 1910 fiscal year). The same man is likely; not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate. Most history comes from Lighthouse Friends (facts only, restated in our own words, apart from one quoted sentence). Checked on the page images: the fiscal 1910 keeper table (printed p. 253, scan p. 255) reads 'Tignish Run | Agape Gaudet | Aug. 30, 1897 | 150'; the fiscal 1908 statement (printed p. 176, scan p. 185) has the same station, keeper and date with salary 130. The fiscal 1912 agency list (printed p. 58, scan p. 65) shows 'Big Tignish range' as a station name; keeper columns were not used. The Department's reports before 1900 are not in our corpus, so the 1877 and 1881 dates rest on Lighthouse Friends alone. The 1887 date for the front light's loss is inferred from the 1888 text ('the previous fall'). The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights and the Lighthouse Directory were not read. The record's 'active' status is not confirmed here. No wreck or rescue tied to this light was found. Lighthouse Friends' text names the last keeper 'Alphonse Gaude' and its keeper list 'Alphonse Gaudet'.
